entries.title: DynaVelo predicts regulatory perturbations from single-cell multiomics
entries.summary: DynaVelo learns joint RNA-expression and transcription-factor motif dynamics with a neural differential-equation model, enabling in silico perturbations of germinal-center B cells. Predicted rescue targets for Arid1a loss were tested in mice, supporting a route from multiomic trajectories to experimentally testable regulatory hypotheses.
entries.access: Publisher article and metadata

entries.title: HitSV detects structural variants across sequencing technologies
entries.summary: HitSV combines repeat-aware breakpoint detection with haplotype-resolved local assembly to reconstruct and genotype structural variants from short, long or hybrid reads. Reported benchmark and cohort results make it a candidate for variant-pipeline evaluation, with performance dependent on the sequencing and genomic contexts tested.
entries.access: Publisher article and metadata

entries.title: Targeted lipid nanoparticles generate CAR NK cells in vivo
entries.summary: Ligand-directed lipid nanoparticles deliver CAR messenger RNA to natural killer cells, with antitumor effects demonstrated in preclinical models. The study offers a nonviral cell-engineering strategy, but mouse and humanized-model results do not establish safety or effectiveness in patients.
entries.access: Publisher abstract/visible preview and metadata only

entries.title: ATLAS scales spatial cell mapping using learned transcriptional signatures
entries.summary: ATLAS learns signatures from single-cell RNA-seq references and decodes them from tissue measurements to infer cell types and transcriptomes. Profiling millions of mouse-brain cells demonstrates comparative mapping across genetic backgrounds, while imputed expression should be distinguished from directly measured genes.
entries.access: Publisher abstract/visible preview and metadata only

entries.title: VIMA tests disease-associated microniches in spatial molecular data
entries.summary: VIMA learns continuous tissue-patch representations and tests overlapping microniches for associations with case–control status, avoiding reliance on a fixed set of cell types or tissue regions. Simulations and applications across three diseases evaluate calibration and power, offering a framework for study-level spatial comparisons.
entries.access: Publisher article and metadata

entries.title: Spatial transcriptomics benchmark compares 11 segmentation methods
entries.summary: This study compares 11 segmentation methods across 15 datasets from five spatial technologies using metrics for transcript recovery, expression purity, morphology and downstream interpretation. A shared Nextflow evaluation pipeline supports method selection, with results emphasizing context-dependent trade-offs rather than a universally best segmentation tool.
entries.access: Publisher article and metadata

entries.title: Tangermeme supports interpretation of genomic deep-learning models
entries.summary: Tangermeme provides composable sequence manipulation, feature attribution and motif-analysis tools for using trained genomic models. Its checks for problematic attribution convergence and reusable analysis components can make regulatory-sequence studies easier to inspect and reproduce.
entries.access: Publisher article and metadata

entries.title: JEEPERS corrects jagged-end artifacts in cfDNA methylation analysis
entries.summary: JEEPERS identifies and corrects methylation errors introduced when jagged cell-free DNA ends are repaired during library preparation. Evaluations in cancer-related profiling illustrate joint methylation and mutation analysis, but clinical deployment requires further validation and the software carries a noncommercial research license.
entries.access: Publisher article and metadata

entries.title: AmpliconSuite analyzes focal amplification and ecDNA in cancer genomes
entries.summary: AmpliconSuite organizes whole-genome sequencing analysis of focal amplifications, including extrachromosomal DNA and breakage–fusion–bridge structures. Orthogonal validation and pan-cancer analyses accompany AmpliconRepository, a shared resource for exploring amplification results across thousands of samples.
entries.access: Publisher article and metadata

entries.title: CauTrigger prioritizes candidate drivers of biological state transitions
entries.summary: CauTrigger uses hierarchical latent-variable modeling to separate proposed causal signals from confounding variation and predict perturbation outcomes across regulatory layers. Applications to single-cell multiomics generate testable hypotheses; causal interpretation remains dependent on modeling assumptions and experimental follow-up.
entries.access: Publisher abstract/visible preview and metadata only

entries.title: Thyra connects mass spectrometry imaging with SpatialData
entries.summary: Thyra converts raw vendor and imzML mass-spectrometry imaging data into the SpatialData ecosystem. This provides a practical route to combining molecular imaging with histology and spatial transcriptomics while reducing fragmentation across data formats.
entries.access: Publisher abstract/visible preview and metadata only

entries.title: OpenDVP links image analysis and spatial proteomics in archival tissues
entries.summary: OpenDVP combines open image-analysis tools with AnnData and SpatialData in an experimental and computational workflow for deep visual proteomics. Demonstrations in placenta, lung cancer and relapsed breast cancer connect spatial cell phenotypes with exploratory proteomic measurements and neighborhood profiling.
entries.access: Publisher article and metadata

entries.title: MassNet supplies a large standardized corpus for proteomics AI
entries.summary: MassNet curates 1.5 billion tandem mass spectra across 35 species and introduces a tensor format for reusable proteomics training data. The study demonstrates de novo peptide sequencing and other learning tasks, providing a resource for benchmarking models rather than guaranteeing performance on every instrument or sample type.
entries.access: Publisher article and metadata

entries.title: Self-supervised models benchmark morphological profiling of perturbations
entries.summary: A large Cell Painting study compares self-supervised image representations against classical morphological profiling and releases pretrained models. Held-out evaluations show gains for selected architectures across perturbations and cell types, offering alternatives to segmentation-based feature extraction with dataset-specific performance limits.
entries.access: Publisher article and metadata

entries.title: CopilotJ connects conversational agents with ImageJ workflows
entries.summary: CopilotJ links language-model agents to ImageJ through a bidirectional plugin for planning and executing bioimage analyses. Validated pipelines can be saved for batch processing, while the reported task and synthetic-image evaluations do not remove the need to inspect scientific outputs.
entries.access: Publisher abstract/visible preview and metadata only

entries.title: Detectrons record transient RNA signals as DNA barcodes
entries.summary: Detectrons couple programmable RNA sensing with retron-mediated reverse transcription to create durable DNA records of transcriptional events. Multiplexed phage-detection experiments in bacteria demonstrate sequencing-based recording, with mammalian or clinical applications outside the demonstrated scope.
entries.access: Publisher abstract/visible preview and metadata only

coverage_lessons: Use the public WordPress REST API as a fallback for RNA-seq Blog. It returned all 47 October posts and X-WP-Total=47 / X-WP-TotalPages=1 while HTML archives failed. Request date, date_gmt, modified, link, title and content; use original date for eligibility and strip style/script text before reading content.

For Nature journals, enumerate the year archive without an article-type filter and follow pages until both date boundaries are crossed. Brief Communications, Analyses, Resources and Correspondence include relevant methods. Verify first online publication on the article itself, not its issue date.
Use topic searches to supplement a dated inventory, not to declare journal coverage complete. This expanded pass recovered 37 Nature Methods and 34 Nature Biotechnology October listings.

Keep both blog and paper dates. scFlowReport (September), Unify (July) and the nanopore review (March) qualify through substantive October coverage; never relabel those primary studies as first published in October.

Primary bibliographic services can expose issue-level or incomplete dates. Prefer publisher first-online metadata or Crossref published-online over generic published/print dates, and record disagreements. A verified blog date can independently establish eligibility.
A readable current RSS feed is not a historical archive: Planet Python’s fetched feed contained only November. Record its actual date span.
Verify release timestamps for newsletter discoveries. The unresolved MCP issuer-security lead was September software, despite October newsletter coverage.
